newsitem.title: USA: Teamsters set Sunday night UPS strike deadline.
newsitem.headline: Teamsters set Sunday night UPS strike deadline.

text.p: The Teamsters Union on Saturday set a new strike deadline for Sunday at midnight in its dispute with United Parcel Service, the largest U.S. package carrier.

"More than 185,000 Teamster members at United Parcel Service will go on strike on Sunday night at midnight EDT (0400 GMT on Monday) if the company refuses to agree to a new contract that provides good full-time jobs with pensions and health coverage," the union said in a statement.

Talks between the union and UPS were put on hold on Friday night, after a strike deadline passed at midnight on Thursday. No time was set for resuming negotiations, and a Teamsters spokesman said it was up to the company to respond before Sunday night to avert a strike.
"We're prepared to meet up until the deadline," said Teamsters spokesman Rand Wilson.

UPS had no immediate comment on the new strike deadline. "We have not received anything formally from the Teamsters yet," said spokeswoman Gina Ellrich. "We are waiting to be contacted by the (federal) mediators."

Teamsters president Ron Carey said the union was holding out for a contract that shifted more workers into full-time jobs, limited the company's ability to subcontract drivers' jobs, improved pension benefits, and improved health and safety standards.
"The brown trucks won't be rolling unless this company agrees to provide the good jobs that American families need," Carey said in a statement.

UPS said it was losing about $5 million a day in business, with about 1 million packages a day going to other services as the prospect of a strike grew. The company normally delivers about 12 million packages daily.

"The trend that we've seen from our customers (is) the closer we got to the deadline the more they diverted their volume," said Ellrich. "We think the more tenuous it is, the more we will see that happen."
The company said it had already had to start laying off workers temporarily.

UPS is the largest package carrier in the United States, with 1996 revenues of $22.4 billion. It handles 3.15 billion parcels and documents, shipped annually to more than 200 countries from 1,700 hubs and centers.
Federal mediator John Calhoun Wells was not available for comment.
